title: Observations of the temporal evolution of Saturn's stratosphere following the Great Storm of 2010─2011: II. Latitudinal distribution of CO and stratospheric winds
question: Assess whether Saturn's 2010-2011 stratospheric beacon perturbed the CO distribution and measure how the vortex perturbed the stratospheric wind regime.

what.value: Seasonal altitude-latitude thermal field retrieved from Cassini/CIRS measurements

evidence.quote: For the SMA data from March 2010, we use the seasonal altitude-latitude thermal field retrieved from Cassini/CIRS measurements presented in (cite: Fletcher2018b).

what.value: Temperatures retrieved from beacon-specific observations on January 27, 2012, and beacon western drift

evidence.quote: (ii) temperatures retrieved as a function of altitude, latitude, and longitude from beacon-specific observations carried out on January 27, 2012, by (cite: Fletcher2012b).

what.value: Physical vertical profile of CO from a ~220-year-old comet impact

evidence.loc: Background composition and CO distribution model
evidence.quote: we choose to adopt the physical profile of (cite: Cavalie2010) derived from atmospheric transport following a comet impact occurring $\sim$220 years before the observations

what.value: Line broadening parameters for NH3, PH3, and CO

evidence.quote: We have computed the line broadening parameters following (cite: Fletcher2007) for NH$_3$, (cite: Levy1993; Levy1994) for PH$_3$, and (cite: Dick2009) for CO.

what.value: 2018 ALMA stratospheric wind measurements of Saturn

evidence.quote: The measurements confirm the presence of the broad prograde equatorial jet initially detected by (cite: Benmahi2022; Benmahi2025) in the stratosphere.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, concatenate, and image ALMA visibility data
recipe.method: Calibrate bandpass, gain, phase, and flux; rescale uv distances and amplitudes of Jan 22 data to match Jan 14 apparent size and total flux; concatenate measurement sets; perform self-calibration, visibility continuum subtraction, and multiscale clean.
key_parameters: multiscale scale 1" for limb spectral data
assumptions: No line emission in the rings

recipe.goal: Extract limb spectra and remove residual baseline ripples
recipe.method: Apply pointing offset correction (+0.27" RA, +0.33" Dec for ALMA), extract spectra along the 1-bar planetary limb oversampling the synthesized beam by a factor of 4, and remove standing waves using sine waves or polynomial fits.
key_parameters: beam oversampling factor of 4; pointing offset +0.27" RA, +0.33" Dec (ALMA); primary beam correction factor 1.25 (SMA)

recipe.goal: Model radiative transfer and derive CO meridional distribution
recipe.method: Use a 3D line-by-line radiative transfer model with Cassini/CIRS thermal fields and scale a 220-year-old comet impact vertical profile to fit limb spectra and derive CO mole fraction at 0.3 mbar.
key_parameters: N=30 spectral points for SMA, N=100 for ALMA; selection threshold chi^2/N < 9 (and < 4)
assumptions: Tropospheric CO (1.2 ppb) is neglected; temperatures expanded isothermally upward of 0.2 mbar

recipe.goal: Retrieve stratospheric winds from Doppler shifts of ALMA limb spectra
recipe.method: Fit a parametrized analytical function to observed CO lines within +/-1.5 MHz of the line peak to measure Doppler shifts, subtract beam-convolved planet rotation, and deproject line-of-sight velocities to zonal wind speeds.
key_parameters: Fitting frequency range within +/- 1.5 MHz of line peak; sub-Earth latitude 15.1 deg N
assumptions: Systematic uncertainty of ~50 m/s caused by spectral baseline removal

answer_key.quantity: Prograde jet velocity at 50 deg S

evidence.quote: We can identify two prograde jets, centered around 50$^\circ$S and 40$^\circ$S, with speeds of 135$\pm$60 m.s$^{-1}$ and 210$\pm$60 m.s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Prograde jet velocity at 40 deg S

evidence.quote: We can identify two prograde jets, centered around 50$^\circ$S and 40$^\circ$S, with speeds of 135$\pm$60 m.s$^{-1}$ and 210$\pm$60 m.s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Equatorial prograde jet slowing relative to 2018

evidence.quote: The equatorial prograde jet is 100 to 200 m.s$^{-1}$ slower, and broader in latitude, than in quiescent conditions.

answer_key.quantity: Beacon anticyclonic wind peak speed on eastern limb (33-47 deg N)

evidence.quote: The peaks are symmetric in speed with values of 60$\pm$15 m.s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Retrograde flow speed on western limb (30-45 deg N)

evidence.quote: On the opposite limb, the winds are tentatively found retrograde with an average speed of -50$\pm$20 m.s$^{-1}$ between 30$^\circ$N and 45$^\circ$N.

answer_key.quantity: Prograde jet velocity at 50-67 deg N

evidence.quote: A broad 140$\pm$45 m.s$^{-1}$ prograde jet, not seen in the thermal wind of (cite: Fletcher2012b) but evident as very strong windshear in Fig. 4 of (cite: Fletcher2018b), extends from 50$^\circ$N to 67$^\circ$N.

answer_key.quantity: Retrograde polar jet peak velocity at 74 deg N

evidence.quote: except a narrower retrograde jet that is located around 74$^\circ$N with a peak velocity of -220$\pm$80 m.s$^{-1}$.

not_stated_but_needed: Visibility weighting scheme (e.g., Briggs robust parameter) used during ALMA imaging
Image pixel/cell size and image dimensions for ALMA and SMA cubes
Self-calibration solution intervals and number of iterations for ALMA data
Exact list of multiscale clean scales used for continuum imaging
Specific parameters of the sine wave / polynomial fits used for baseline ripple removal on each extracted spectrum
missing_for_reproduction: Proprietary/in-house 3D radiative transfer code (Cavalié et al. 2019) and wind retrieval code (Cavalié et al. 2021)
2D/3D Cassini/CIRS temperature grids from Fletcher et al. (2012b, 2018b) formatted for the radiative transfer model
Exact polynomial/sine baseline subtraction parameters per limb position
Detailed CASA self-calibration and clean scripts (masks, cell size, weighting, multiscale parameters)
score_reason: The ALMA data are public (Cycle 0 project 2011.0.00808.S) and the high-level methodology and key numerical results are clearly presented, but reproduction requires in-house radiative transfer and wind-retrieval codes, external Cassini/CIRS thermal grids, and manual per-spectrum baseline ripple fitting parameters that are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Public Cycle 0 ALMA data with clear numeric targets (zonal wind velocities as a function of latitude and mean limb CO abundance); an agent could independently image the cube, extract limb spectra, and measure the Doppler shift profile to rediscover the equatorial jet slowing and high-latitude jets without needing the proprietary radiative transfer code.
